issues.issue: The fund schedules break this line down (p9: Activity Fund 123,737 activities receipts + School Nutrition 2,451 private grants; p10: rentals 3,304, license fees/fines 1,650, donations 5,276, other 825). Activity receipts make up 90% of it, so under the mixed-line rule it should take the dominant category, charges for services/fees, with a review note naming the mix. 'other' is a last resort and doesn't fit here.

The category list has 'student activities' for activity funds. The statement (p4, p9) reports this spending under Support services - pupils, so the extractor's choice is defensible and already marked review, but 'student activities' may be intended.
These are county-collected fines and license fees passed to the school. Treating them as county/other local governments money is defensible, but 'fines and forfeitures' could also apply.

issues.on_page: School Nutrition Fund shown as a nonmajor governmental fund (receipts 68,148, disbursements 112,622)
issues.issue: The extractor rules give school nutrition as an example of a business-type fund. This report presents it as governmental and the extraction follows the report. That is consistent with the statements, but it departs from the rules' default.
